events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
For the following areas...
S of Oregon Inlet NC to Cape Hatteras NC out to 20 NM...
Waters from Oregon Inlet to Cape Hatteras NC from 20 to 60 NM...

At 1200 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 20 nm southeast of
Rodanthe, moving east at 30 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to nearly 50 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Hazardous temperatures in excess of 100 degrees are
forecast to develop Monday afternoon across valley locations in
northwest Utah, particularly along the northern Wasatch Front and
the Great Salt Lake Desert.

* WHERE...Eastern Box Elder County, Great Salt Lake Desert and
Mountains, Northern Wasatch Front, Salt Lake Valley, and Tooele
and Rush Valleys.

* WHEN...From noon Monday to midnight MDT Monday Night.

* IMPACTS...Low temperatures into Monday morning will stay elevated
in the upper 60s to mid 70s for most lower valley locations,
offering little relief overnight.

events.region: Dickey, ND
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1055 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 7 miles southwest
of Merricourt City, or 17 miles northwest of Ellendale, moving east
at 35 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect considerable
tree damage. Wind damage is also likely to mobile homes,
roofs, and outbuildings.

Locations impacted include...
Ellendale, Fullerton, Forbes, Merricourt City, Monango and
Merricourt.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Mohave, AZ
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Central Mohave County in northwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1030 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 855 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Diamond Creek Campground, Windy Point Campground, Packsaddle
Campground, Dolan Springs and Peach Springs.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Anson, NC; Hoke, NC; Montgomery, NC; Moore, NC; Richmond, NC; Scotland, NC; Stanly, NC
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of central North Carolina, including the
following counties, Anson, Hoke, Montgomery, Moore, Richmond,
Scotland and Stanly.

* WHEN...Until 400 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1147 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a large area of
showers and thunderstorms causing heavy rainfall. Many
locations across the Sandhills have seen intermittent periods
of heavy rain since late Sunday evening, and this is likely
to continue through the early morning hours. Between 2 and 3
inches of rain have fallen since 8 PM Sunday. Minor flooding
is expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected
over the area through 4 AM Monday. This additional rain will
result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Laurinburg, Southern Pines, Rockingham, Wadesboro, Raeford,
Carthage, Pinehurst, Hamlet, Aberdeen, Biscoe, Ansonville,
Hoffman, Antioch, Polkton, Locust, Whispering Pines, Norwood,
Oakboro, Stanfield and Pinebluff.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
